label: Reed
terms_note: Jobseeker API (search + job details, basic-auth key). Applications need the Reed account form — assisted for apply.

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes** (Jobseeker search + details API, no apply).
auth: 1. Register on the developer portal ("Sign up for a reed.co.uk API key") — free.
2. Every request: HTTP Basic auth with the API key as the user name and an empty password.
3. No OAuth, no user context — the key identifies the developer, not the job seeker.

endpoints.notes: employerId, employerName, jobTitle, jobDescription (HTML), locationName, min/max salary, yearlyMinimum/Maximum, currency, salaryType, datePosted, expirationDate, externalUrl, jobUrl, applications count, contractType, fullTime/partTime

reference.limits: Not published on the developer pages; `resultsToTake` is capped at 100 per call. - Free developer key; no separate API terms text was found on the jobseeker pages (the portal only says to register). - Search/details only — nothing in the API acts on a job seeker's account, so no automated-application question arises.

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: Reed Jobseeker API key from https://www.reed.co.uk/developers/jobseeker; sent as the HTTP Basic user name with an empty password.

me.note: Verified with a one-result search (Reed has no account endpoint).

not_offered.apply: Reed's Jobseeker API has no application endpoint; candidates apply on reed.co.uk.

evidence: host www.reed.co.uk: DNS ok, TLSv1.2 (Google Trust Services)
probe: 3/3 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 404 (not_found), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 3/3 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages; every parameter and body key named on the page
